correctness.rationale: The exact GF(2) argument M=I+A shows Mx=1 is solvable: for y in ker(M), y·1=yᵀMy=yᵀAy=0 in characteristic two. Selected-vertex induced degree is even, and vertex-disjoint simple cycles prohibit Eulerian degree >=4; hence selected degrees 0/2 and unselected degrees positive odd meet the stated rule. Both seven-vertex examples have explicit center-action contradictions. An independently written integer exhaustive census enumerated all 2^(n choose 2) labelled simple graphs (n<=6) and all n=7 graphs of possible cactus edge sizes 6..9, checked biconnected components, every action profile and explicit adjacency permutations. Counts were n=1..7: 1,1,4,31,362,5676,111982; failures 0 through n=6 and 3150 at n=7, exactly two isomorphism types with multiplicities 630 and 2520. The analytic existence lemma extends beyond finite n; finite enumeration alone would not prove it.
residual_risks: No classification of all cactus obstructions at n>7; structural existence only for vertex-disjoint cycles and stated T odd values.
